image_description: Two adult male mallard ducks (drakes) standing in shallow water. The duck on the left is fully visible, displaying characteristic breeding plumage: iridescent green head, white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/brown body with a blue speculum patch on the wing. The duck on the right is partially occluded by the left duck, showing similar plumage but with the head turned away or obscured. Both have orange webbed feet visible in the water. The background consists of rippling greenish water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left drake clearly displays a broad, flat, yellow-green bill consistent with mallard anatomy. The right drake's bill is not clearly visible due to angle/occlusion.
The left drake has a visible dark eye. The right drake's eye is obscured.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Both subjects exhibit the characteristic stocky, streamlined body shape of a duck. Plumage appears dense and textured correctly for water resistance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left drake perfectly matches the mallard description: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey/flank feathers. The right drake shows matching brown/chestnut tones.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Orange legs are visible on both ducks. The left duck's foot is partially submerged but shows the correct orange color and general webbed structure. No anatomical errors like extra toes or fused limbs are visible.
The folded wings on the left drake show the correct aerodynamic shape and the distinctive blue speculum patch bordered by white, typical of mallards.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tails of both ducks are either cut off by the frame or obscured by the other duck/water angle. The characteristic 'drake curl' is not clearly visible on either subject.
